legend: For his next video, Mr. Beast has gathered n%%ZSMJ0%% contestants on his private planet Island, which, fittingly, is an ocean planet with a single large island. Each contestant is given two numbers ai%%ZSMJ1%% and bi%%ZSMJ2%%, which are the beginning and end of a sequence of consecutive numbers that the contestant has to count, in order. For a prize of 1 trillion dollars, the contestants have to work together to ensure that each contestant counts their own numbers while maintaining a nondecreasing order between all the contestants' numbers.

Now, the contestants need your help to answer q%%ZSMJ3%% queries asking for the numbers that will be counted at various positions. In other words, each query asks for the number at a specific position in the sorted list containing all the sequences merged together.
input: The first line of input contains n%%ZSMJ4%% and q%%ZSMJ5%% (1≤n,q≤105%%ZSMJ6%%), the number of sequences and the number of queries, respectively.

The next n%%ZSMJ7%% lines each contain two integers ai%%ZSMJ8%% and bi%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤ai≤bi≤109%%ZSMJ10%%), the beginning and end (inclusive) of the ith%%ZSMJ11%% sequence of consecutive numbers, respectively.
The next line contains q%%ZSMJ12%% integers x1,x2,...,xn%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤xi≤1014%%ZSMJ14%%), the position that each query asks about in the sorted list; each position is guaranteed to be valid.
output: The output should be q%%ZSMJ15%% integers, each on a separate line, the number counted at each query's position.
note: The three given sequences are 1,2,3%%ZSMJ16%%; 2,3,4%%ZSMJ17%%; and 3,4,5%%ZSMJ18%%. When merged together and sorted, the result is 1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,5%%ZSMJ19%%. The queries ask for every index in order, so the whole list is printed.
